text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.25% today to $140.50, extending a four-day decline from its November 13 peak of $142.28. The pullback aligns with a slight softening in crude oil prices—US oil dropped below $90 per barrel (now at $89.62), and global prices are at $92.14. Even modest crude weakness can pressure oil majors' near-term valuations, particularly after the stock had climbed steadily through mid-November.

The two-week decline of 4.3% is worth noting in context: heating oil prices are up 59% year-over-year, which typically benefits refiners and integrated oil companies, yet the broader market appears to be pricing in caution around winter demand and consumer spending. Rising energy costs (reflected in shipping and heating concerns) could dampen economic activity heading into the holidays, which may explain why the stock retreated despite favorable fundamentals for the energy sector.
